Like how how often does that go through your mind? >> I mean, you really have no idea. It's constant. It's the second you wake up in the morning, I turn the shower on. >> [clears throat and cough] >> All I think about when I'm in the shower is what this team what what we want for this team next year. And um I have to keep notes in my phone of things I want to tweak about the schedule. And so it's a constant I mean, I spend time with my family. I think I do a good job separating that, you know, when I'm with them, but um I think if you were in my brain, it's just a constant constant thought that's going on on things that we got to do, things we got to tweak, where we need to be. Um so yeah, it's it's that's our expectation is is to be great and play for games that are really meaningful at the end of the year. We haven't done that recently, and we know what it looks like and feels like. That's the good news. And I think we got a lot of guys that understand that as well and this coaching staff that understands it, and we're going to do everything we can to get there. >> We don't talk about Tee Higgins a ton. How do you feel like he's grown as this is one of the things that's going to be like what, his seventh for him here? How do you feel like he's kind of grown, especially over the last year and and his role in the offense? >> Um I I'm I like Tee a lot. How has he grown specifically? It's hard. I I do think there's a lot of leadership qualities to him. He goes about his business. He's the same personality every day when he walks in the building. That's big for me. And he's he's so difficult to defend. He's such a rare athlete. I know there's a lot of big receivers out there, but he is he's long. He's got tremendous speed. He's got tremendous hands. He's a really high football IQ. He's been in the same system for a long time with the same quarterback. Um so there's just an expectation that he has and a standard he has for himself that he wants to meet all the time. And so I don't think he's I'm not I'm not going to sit here and say I'm proud of what he's done because he came in um with the right attitude from from the jump, you know, he was a national champion in college, so he had high expectations there. And so again, he's he's uh one of those guys you love coaching, you love being around. >> This gap in the NFL schedule between mini camp and training camp, uh any message to the guys about how to handle the next 5 weeks or so individually? >> Well, it's they got to come back ready to roll, you know? And so you put in all this work, and you can't just waste all the work you put in. Whether schematically or whether it's individually in your body. But that's on us to bring in the right guys that you don't have as much concern. It's hard when you got 90 guys, but I think what Duke and his staff done a really good job of bringing in guys that understand what our purpose is here. And if you understand what our purpose is, then I don't have to hold your hand for the next 5 weeks. You're going to show up ready to go. And if you're not, it'll be exposed in the first 4 days of training camp. You know, and so I think that's very simple. And of course, over 7 years, you see guys that fall into that category and often times don't don't survive the whole course of the season for one reason or another. So these guys that we brought in are all about the right stuff, and and I expect them to come back ready to go. >> How much monitoring are you able to do over this time? Or or is is is there a high level of like keeping up with guys monitoring or is it >> No, I know. They they need some time away from us. So yeah, there there's some checkpoints with position coaches just just to see how the guys are doing, what their travels are. Um but yeah, let them be. They they don't want to hear They've heard from us every second of every day the last how many weeks. And so, you give them time. They're going to be with us for 6 more months every single day, every single hour. So, you'll give them time and space and I need that from them as well. So, I think everybody's having the same understanding. >> A lot of the players, you know, take this time to maybe go on a little vacation and then, you know, get back to to work. Do you take any time off in this time or are you just, you know, focused on getting ready for for training camp in the season? >> I get to spend time with my family. Um I've got basketball pick-up today at 3:00. I got two pick-ups. I got one at 2:00 and one at 3:00. So, I'll be at both of those. And then, uh that's the stuff I enjoy. I enjoy being at sporting events with my kids. I enjoy throwing the football in the backyard. I enjoy uh teaching and McLaren how to serve an overhand volley. I don't know how to do it, but I act like I do. Um so, uh those are the things that I finally get a chance to relax, you know, wake up with my wife, have a cup of coffee, stress-free, don't got to get in the office. So, um and then we'll then we'll spend time and get away for a couple days. But for the most part, I like being in Cincinnati. It's it's the time I get to enjoy at my house without, you know, always going to work. I've got spots in my house I can do it, but um I do look forward to just being with my family and and enjoying the life we have. >> This time of year, um when guys, you know, mini camp is when guys can maybe in the off-season let themselves go a little bit physically. But you showed up here in really good shape. I mean, everybody's serious about, you know, this stuff coming season. Um it's also a time I remember when I played was a time where you start bonding with guys. I mean, you really start to form pretty decent relationships. How important is all that? >> It's it's important and that a lot of that Yeah, it's on us as coaches to create the chemistry and the bonding opportunities. And it's on the players to take it off the field as well. And um I think that they've done an excellent job this off-season. I I know of several guys that have gone out of their way to make sure everybody feels included and feels like they get an opportunity to know each other and I don't think that's over yet. Um so I think that's good and you know, also guys taking care of themselves. I also think we have a tremendous strength and conditioning crew. You know, Joey Bosa, Garrett Swanson, Diamond. Um those guys, I think the players really respect them and trust them and uh they've they've operated at a high level for a long time and so they've done a great job helping those guys maintain, getting in shape, getting in shape and when we come back in training camp, they'll be a big part of getting those guys ready to go. >> What similarities do you see if any from this year's group in this spring compared to the Super Bowl run and in that spring? >> I I'm careful to compare so far back. It just starts with the leadership. I feel good about the leadership and I think sometimes you might talk yourself into feeling that way. I I genuinely you know, I spend a lot of time on you know, who could potential captains be. There there's a lot of opportunity there. There's there's a lot of candidates. That's a good thing. You're not having to talk yourself into who it could be. Um it'll take shape the right way, but just pleased with the attitude those guys have brought, how they've helped others get better and so I think we got a lot of good guys that way. >> All right, we're going to wrap this up cuz it sounds like Joe's ready to go. >> Sounds like I think >> Thank you so much for your questions. >> Should I go Should I go to the time? Thank you.

title: Bengals Star Dexter Lawrence on State of Defense, Mindset After Minicamp
text: So, let's just put a bow on this off season. How was it being here with the Bengals and getting ready for training camp in a few weeks? >> Um, it was fun. Um, obviously a big adjustment. Uh, you know, moving and moving to a new city and all that, but you know, guys welcome me in, introduced me to the right people, made it made it really good. >> What are you looking forward to the most about just getting training camp started here? >> Um, just growing with the guys. Um, you know, putting in hard work and and grinding and u, you know, preparing for the season. and it's a process that that we're going to enjoy. >> Been like working with some of these younger guys on this Bengals team. I know we've seen you talking to a lot of them, helping them. How has that been for you? >> Uh good. I mean, it's it's part it's part of my role. Um you know, to to allow people to understand my knowledge of the game and and to grow in that sense. So, I think um it just it just it just happens naturally type of thing. So, I'm just excited to keep go growing with them and and learning. How much have you felt the energy of this city of your teammates since you got here a few months ago? >> Um, well, I I don't know if I felt felt it. They kind of said that everybody else said it changed. Um, but that's just how it was when I got here. So, I'm embracing it and I and I enjoy it. Um, you know, it's just it's just about winning and doing what you can to win and doing what you can to help everybody else around you be successful. these uh OTAAS workouts that you had before now one day a mandatory mini camp. What are you making of this group of uh coach Montgomery, everyone that you're working with? >> Um that everybody has a has a purpose and and everybody has the same goal and that's it's just winning and doing what you can to win. And I'm excited about that. You know, Coach McGomery, he um you know, he's a perfectionist and he wants everything to be to a te and I respect that a lot. Um he's intentional with his work and it's it's going to be exciting. >> I asked you about the energy that that your teammates have had. Does the the change of scenery for you rejuvenate you give you some some juice going into this season? >> Um I think for me it's just continuing who I am as a player and um I love this game and I and I and I give my all to this game. So the juice will never die. Um it's just more of just how you know how I can positively impact the team. Have you adjusted to like being here in Cincinnati yet, do you feel? >> It gives me a little southern vibe. Um, which which I enjoy. Uh, so it's been fun. It's been fun learning about the city and I probably won't try the Chile. Uh, but it's been good and um, like I said, like a lot of guys have helped me adjust and and introduce me to the right people. >> Now that you all are headed out, what do the next five weeks or so look like for you? >> Don't be like a boxer. you know, when it before they going to they fight, you got to put your head down and train. That's what it's about. >> So, and so the next five weeks for you are not in any way about rest or anything like that. It's about go time. >> Yeah, it's go time. >> It's go time right now in June. >> Yeah. >> That's the process. >> Hey, is that something you've learned over the course of your career? >> That's something that's something I've been doing since my rookie year. you know, around this time the before we get back, I just put my head down and I go to work and get ready for camp. >> Sir, do you do you feel like you're in the middle of your prime? >> Um, I I don't really know, man. I I just I just come out I just come show up every day with joy and it goes fast. I'm already in year eight. Um, and you know, I guess people can say that's prime, but I feel good and you know, I just keep learning every day. I take it I take it a process. It's a process for me um every year that that the season ends and this my process and I just want to keep growing and and learning my position and you know I'm here now to to be an impact and you know I'm just going to continue to prove who I am and you know help this team. >> How did they tell you all that the rest of mini camp was being called off and what was the reaction from the guys? >> Um just in a team meeting uh just now before we went outside for a little bit. Um, so it was, you know, I don't know if guys are excited. You know, we love, I think we love being out here with around each other and but obviously the wait time can help us, you know, rejuvenate and get our minds right. So, it's a it's a it's a plus minus thing. >> What kind of attitude do you need to see in this locker room from the other guys when you all show up in late July? >> Um, just a sense of urgency um to to grow and and to and you know, unselfishness. Don't be selfish. um just to grow in your position and and your knowledge and and intensity at practice every day to go out and you know and just to get 1% better. That's cliche, but I think that's the biggest thing. You either grew during practice or you got worse.

title: Chris O'Leary On Setting The Standard At Minicamp | LA Chargers
text: Overall thoughts on on spring so far and mini camp? >> Yeah, excited. Um really proud of where we're at right now. Um obviously have a long way to go going into fall camp in the season, but our plan going into it, uh you know, looking back at where we're at now, I think we've accomplished what we set out to accomplish. Um and everybody's ready to take a little break and then really launch into it in fall camp. >> What what were those things you were trying to accomplish in the off-season first? >> Uh you know, establish our identity um as a defense. That was kind of step one. Um get our arsenal in, get all our calls in, get get what we want to build through the year, get that ran, get executed. Um and we did that and then really set our standard of defensive play. So, uh how we take the field, how we communicate, how we get off blocks, like all those things. Really establish that in these uh in these OTAs and mini camp. Um and I feel like we feel like we've been able to do that. >> What what is the the identity and the standard? >> Uh you know, the identity for us uh is really a group that plays together, that plays fast and violent. We got a strong brotherhood. Um we believe in unit strength. 11 guys playing together as one is better than 11 guys playing independently. Um so, that's kind of our identity as a group. Um and then the standard is just our separators putting them on display. Uh block destruction, communication, all the things we talk about um and doing that on a consistent basis. >> I guess how how is that different from just from what you guys were doing last year? >> I don't I don't know how to comment on that really. Like I wasn't here last year. Um so, I don't know the difference is. Um similar. >> I guess your statement of it, I mean. >> Uh a lot of what we've spent time on um and I think this applies from Pop Warner football all the way to the NFL. It's like the team that plays together, cares about each other, um does it for reasons that are selfless. Um I think those teams really do special things. Um so, we spent a lot of time trying to build that, trying to build that brotherhood, that bond. Um so I'd say that's one thing that's a little bit different that we've been doing. >> Chris, what was the collaborative process been with the players given that, like Chris mentioned, you have been there with them on the staff before, knowing what they've been doing, what they've been asked to do, to now putting your stamp on it and and kind of working differently now? >> Uh extremely collaborative. Um I think we have the best coaches in the world. I think they're experts in their positions. Um I truly mean that. So I've relied heavily on them. Um I view them as the head coaches of their positions. Uh they have input in how we defend the pass, how we defend the run. Um and so it's been extremely collaborative. Uh a lot of the things that we have done here, will continue to do. Um and then the ability to evolve and bring some things that are a little bit different, some change-ups, uh some different ways to approach things. I think the open-mindedness of the group has been incredible. Um and everyone wants to win. Like at the end of the day, we want to win. We want to win the Super Bowl. And so everybody knows in order to do that, we got to work together. Um so it's been it's been a lot of fun. >> What about you about Akeem? >> Uh his professionalism. But where does this part of the season play into that? Or is this just laying groundwork for what you guys are going to do in training camp? >> Yeah. Uh laying the groundwork. Um you know, we we've told the guys kind of the way we approach it is the competition for jobs, that begins in fall camp. Um so this this part of the year for us is about uh learning how to be a pro at your position, uh become an elite technician, uh learn multiple jobs, have a better understanding of the concept of the defense, and we're trying to give them the tools to go into that competition fully prepared. Because when you do that, then I think the cream rises to the top, and we find out who the best players are. >> I think the last time we talked, you said the defense was about 30%. Where would we put it at now? >> I'd give it a soft 80%. Everything we wanted to get in is in. We've left some wiggle room for thoughts as we go into season and some game plan specific stuff. But the core of of who we are and what we want to do, it's in and we're rolling. >> We've heard players say that there are some differences. Coach Harbaugh said the same thing yesterday from what they were doing. Because Derwin's so unique, and you can do so much with him, will his role be the same, or are there things that you think you're going to do differently with him? >> Subtle differences. You know, what he's done the last couple years, he's been a all-pro slot corner, nickel, however you want to say it. I see using him the same way. He's going to be a little bit more versatile in the sense of is he to the field, is he to the boundary, is he blitzing, is he covering. We're going to do all those things with him. But as far as him playing closer to the ball, being at the point of attack, like we're going to keep doing those things with him. And we're excited to see what he can do. >> Is that part of the kind of deal for you? Like are there more things that you would like to do with him, but he's just so good at that that you want to kind of keep him there? >> Absolutely. I mean, you you want 11 Derwin James. So, like the answer that is yes, would love to to to do more and all that, but I think at the end of the day, my job is to get our players in position to do what they're best at. And if you're going to put a a scale to like what he's best at, he's the best at that. Like blitzing, owning the perimeter, he's to me the best in the world at doing that. So, we're going to put him in that position as much as we can. >> You're playing Derwin James at nose tackle if you have 11 Derwin James. >> [laughter] >> He's got to gain a little weight, you know. You put You put 100 on him, yeah. >> So, obviously when when Derwin is playing closer to the line of scrimmage, they need a safety next to Elijah Molden on the back end. How competitive are you expecting, >> [snorts] >> you know, that spot to be with, you know, RJ Tony, Genesis, and as we move into training >> Yeah, extremely competitive. Um I get excited thinking about competition and thinking about fall camp. Like we're ready to go right now. Um obviously we're going to take a step back, but like as I look at each position group and especially the safeties, it's going to be fun. It's going to be fun. It's may the best man win. Uh everybody's going to have a a fair opportunity if they're in that world of like, hey, this is these are the five or these are the six, they're going to all get opportunities to compete. Um in the safety room in particular, you got guys that have all different skill sets and we're going to find out uh which one which one stands up and gets to the top of that group. >> You saw Guinness at the pick yesterday. What what did you like about him? >> That the ball skills, the anticipation. Uh he's natural You see it on his film at Arizona, like I think there's a few things at safety that you can't really teach. Uh one's the ability to close in space. Like you either have great feet and you're able to track and all those things. You can You can get better in that area, but that's something you got. And then the second thing is QB anticipation. Like there's there's a feel and a nuance to looking at the quarterback, feeling routes, and knowing where the ball's about to go. Um and he showed that in college and he's had some flashes here in the off-season for us. >> How are you feeling about the corner room? It's a position where you've got guys that have been here for for a minute and also young players, some vets. Position you guys have had to um this off-season. That's a, you know, undrafted free agents. But just how are you feeling about that group this spring? >> Really good. Um it's one of those where like you come in with uh a mindset or a thought of like, hey, this is what the room looks like. This is who you got. And then you put in the work and you get to this point you're like, holy cow, like D-Jack is a He's a player. Like he's a baller. And you look at Tarheeb, Cam, like all these guys, they all have It's kind of like the safety They're They're unique skill sets, but when they're really utilizing that skill set, when D-Jack is covering down the field, like he's elite. And when Cam Hart gets his hands on somebody at the line of scrimmage, he's elite. And so, getting those guys in those positions to do what they're good at, I'm excited about it. And I think it's a healthy competition as well. And I [snorts] think what I've seen from that group is a maturation from when I was here in '24 with Cam and Tarheeb as rookies, um to the the point they're at now, they're true professionals. And so, I have high hopes for that room. >> When you talk about last year, they were they were rotated pretty significantly at that position, like series-to-series. Are you open to doing something like that, or are you more of a believer in like getting a group that you could play consistently? >> Whatever Whatever fits that group the best and our defense the best. I've done it both ways. Um we kind of talked about this last time, like I've done it both ways. So, whatever works. I like guys to feel confident that we have their back. And so, if they make a mistake, they can get a chance to to get a get-back and stay out there. Um but there are times where rotation helps stay fresh, play faster, play looser. So, we'll see how it goes through the year. >> So, along those lines, when you talk about the uniqueness of each player, uh the unique skill skill set of player-to-player, is there room to accommodate all of that, you know, into a game plan in terms of getting not everybody on the field, but consistently getting guys out there? >> Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely. Absolutely. And so is it at the corner position? I mean, I I named three guys, and it's like you're going to play three guys on the field at one time a lot of snaps during the game, whether you're in nickel defense or dime defense or whatever. So, yeah, we're going to utilize all those. Um and then the depth of a defense, the depth of a team, really shows itself as the season goes. Uh so, it's one of those things that people talk about a lot. It's hard to get in the NFL. Um, I do think we have depth and I'm sure a lot of people feel that way at this time of the year, but I think we got guys that are proven that are in the one deep, two deep that can be starters for us. Um, and I think that's going to help us down the line. >> When you mentioned um, that you gave us kind of a specific number with safeties, did you start doing that math in your head already of how are we going to get these things to fit when it comes time to figuring out which ones are on the active roster and do the players, can they feel that depth in some of these rooms and maybe how the positions are going to shake out? >> Uh, in a loose way, but I think primarily right now there's a feeling of hope for each guy that's on the roster and that's how it should be. Um, I think we go into fall camp and whether you're the eighth guy or you're the fourth guy, you know you're going to get a shot to make it. And so, for me, like, yeah, there's a uh, element of hey, we know who our best 15, 20, I don't you generally know who your kind of top top guys are so you start to think about how to use them. How do we use Derwin? Uh, how do we use Tui and K-Mac? And so, you're thinking about that. The rest of it uh, to me is you see how it plays out in the first week or two of fall camp and then start piecing it together. >> You mentioned your conversations with Mike McDaniel, you know, the high-level nature of them and and your competition at practice. [clears throat] Kind of what have you taken, what have you learned from those interactions with Mike? >> Uh, they've been incredible. Just have a resource, uh, one that's going to challenge you every day schematically. Um, so, when we go against them in seven-on-seven or team or whatever, like, you know you're going to be prepared, you're going to be stressed, you're going to be challenged and as a defense that's all you want. You want practice to be as hard or harder than the game. And so, that's kind of step one and step two, he's been a head coach and so, just being able to feel his perspective, talk to him, see why he's doing certain things, how he would approach it. Um, he doesn't hesitate to pop into my office and give me give me nuggets at times, right? Give me some advice or something that he's doing that day, uh, an approach with his unit and I kind of take down like, oh, that's a great idea. I'm going to do that with the defense, too. Um so, it's been awesome to work with Mike. >> How would you say sorry you came to short conversation with them? >> Just the way they Like I laugh cuz I love those guys, and if you've been around and they both have unique personalities, and Tarheeb is like silly at times, and and Cam's like Cam's sometimes an overthinker, and so both of them have really like leveled out, I would say. And the way they approach it every day, they're going to be the best version of themselves. They don't get too high or too low, and I think in the NFL that's such a a strong quality to have because you're going through a 17-week season and playoffs, and so you have to be able to stay consistent regardless of the outside noise, what people are writing about you, saying about you, whatever. You got to be confident in yourself. And so, that self-confidence is what I've seen from both of them. >> Is there like an example of that or a moment maybe for both of them where you kind of thought like, "Oh, they're they're a little bit different than when I was with them a few years ago"? >> 100% like meeting room Tarheeb, like he's asking serious questions. Uh he's engaged, but there's just a a a level to him that's not so up and down. Um and you just see it and you hear it in in the way he approaches meetings. And then Cam for me is like he takes more chances in practice. Um he makes a bad play, he's able to bounce back. And so, for me like just watching those two in those areas shows up. >> What's been like the for you the biggest challenge if any at all being a DC here? >> Um the biggest challenge of being here um >> Maybe something you've learned so far first time. >> I haven't put much thought to that. you know, the way I kind of approach it every day is like as a coach your job is to solve problems, and your job is to take on challenges. And so, I think when I was at Notre Dame or Western or here like every day there's a ton of challenges, and the way you approach them is everything. And so, I enjoy the challenges here. The challenges have been uh coming in, the system's in place. How do we make it ours, right? How do we make it ours? And every day it's just little incremental gains in that in that regard. Um and the approach from me has just been be consistent, be clear and concise, make sure everybody knows what I'm thinking, um and then everything's kind of fallen in place around that. And we got guys that are good dudes, good coaches, good players. Uh so things are going in the right direction. >> You've spent time working with Jim before. In his 20 years as a head coach, he's been identified always power offense. Are Is he and Mike are they more philosophically similar than maybe the outside perception would be based on what you've seen from from what Mike's doing so far? >> Yeah, I think so. I mean, I don't really know the perception of Mike outside. Um I just know from like watching his offense, but they're good at running the ball and I think that falls into like I think in the in the in the beginning of football it's like run the ball, you win the game, and I don't think that's changed much. And I think Mike kind of views it that way, Jim does, and so I think they're aligned. >> Everyone we uh talked to you wrapped about you described like high-level energy. Where Where did that come from for you? >> Uh from me, I mean, if you're if you're asking like the core of me is my faith in Jesus. Like that's like every day I feel like I've been blessed in opportunity. I feel like I'm here to serve people. Um so I as I reset and I center myself every day is like what is there not to be excited about? You know, I'm here to serve others. I'm here to make people help people be the best version of themselves, coaches and players. And so taking that approach every day, um it's never about me. So, you know, I don't get too bogged down when things go wrong or things are things are a struggle. I just take it and go fight every day and have fun with it. >> What do you think of cop and art spring? >> Uh great. Uh we don't have pads on. So it's like, you know, I I have these one-on-one meetings with our guys and I tell them the same thing. I'm like, "Dude, you're doing everything we're asking. You're improving. I'll give you more in fall camp when we got the pads on and I give you some real feedback on your block destruction, your approach, like things like that. But, as of right now, it's been impressive. He's been at everything. He's been focused on improving. The details are improving. His indie work is intentional. So, everything that we've asked of him, he's he's done a great job with. >> Sticking with the um a lot of people see him out there talking on the roster and they just assume, "Oh, yeah, productive Western. That's why he's here." What what Why do you think he didn't get drafted after all that production and >> [clears throat] >> where do you see him fitting in in that room? >> Um I don't know why he didn't get drafted. Um I told people the whole season he's an NFL guy. Uh we we thought about drafting him. You know, it was it was a conversation. Uh we're excited to have him. I think his skill set is unique. He's a really good pass rusher. He's strong. >> Um I think the thing you can't quantify sometimes is somebody's power, their strength and their power like at the point of attack. And I think when we put the pads on, that's going to stand out, right? He can get off. He can pass rush. But, then when the ball's run at him and the tackles addressing him, like they're going to feel his hands. And that's something that really stands out cuz now you can transition to pass. You can stop the run. Um so, we're excited to see him do that. >> He was here a couple years ago but not so much in one of these positions. Just from those experiences with him then and now, just where have you guys seen his growth the most? >> Uh similar to Tarik Blacklock, just a maturity. And I think that's part of like being in the league for for 2 years, 3 years. Um but, the right type of guys doesn't happen for everybody but it happens for the right type of guys. And so, for Tuli, it's been the same. It's like a maturity. He's still He's still got the humor to him and he's still got the great personality. Uh but, there's a level of seriousness and a level um to his a level of serious to his approach, right? Like so, he's in the meeting room and he has a good time but he's also extremely focused on the task at hand. He goes on the field and he's got his personality showing but I mean, you can tell the intentionality, the detail, the aggressiveness with which he attacks everything. Uh to me, that's what has really improved for him. >> [music]

title: NFL Experts Talk J.J. McCarthy & Kyler Murray, Offensive Line, Receiver Depth, GM Nolan Teasley
text: We are back again here in TCO studios for another beat writer round table and I'm really excited. We have a full house today. We've got the athletics Alec Lewis, ESPN's Kevin Seaffort, Purple Insiders Matthew Coller. Guys, this is kind of like your final day before your summer breakish. How we feeling? >> See, we get a little taste. We get a little taste, right, of mini camp. I can't wait to get out there for training camp. I'm ready for football. When we talk about the Vikings and mini camp, a lot of the eyes were on the quarterback room and what's going on there between Kyler Murray, JJ McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Bromer. Matthew, I will start with you. Some of your observations that you've seen from the two that have been at the podium, Kyler Murray and JJ McCarthy. Yeah, I mean I think with JJ and Kyler, they're in two very different places because this is the third year of JJ McCarthy in this offense, whereas Kyler Murray is just coming in and learning it. And I even remember going back to 2022 when Kevin Oonnell got here, how much Kirk Cousins talked about like this is a challenging offense to learn and the wide receivers, Justin Jefferson even referenced it when we talked about him today. So, from an evaluation standpoint, I find it to be really difficult for us to stand and watch practice and say, "Well, this guy's clearly better than that guy because they're in two different spots." But we were looking for progress from Kyler Murray. How does he throw the football? How comfortable does he look? How much communication is going out there? And then for JJ McCarthy, it's how much progress has he made since the last time we we've seen him. And I think for both quarterbacks, there were up days, there were down reps where you would say, I'm not sure really what happened there, but this is why it's called by Kevin Oonnell the learning phase. So, as we try and we get asked all the time, well, who's winning the competition? Like, I don't know that I could tell you that now. I think that they set the stage for that and it looked like Kyler learned a lot along the way and it looked like the arrow was up for JJ McCarthy, but I think that they're going to need training camp to really decide who is getting the lead, who is performing better on each one of these reps that they get. >> Now, you're shaking your head thinking, yeah, they need training camp to help this decision. >> Yeah, I mean, I think why not? Why not have I mean Kevin Okonnell entered this entire process believing that the competition would ignite the best out of both players and ignite the best out of the team. And so to take it in to training camp where there is where there are actual pads where um there are those competitive you know reps where Brian Flores is calling whatever Brian Flores can call which is essentially everything. Um, like I don't see why that wouldn't be sensible to maximize ultimately what they can be and what the team can be. >> Yeah. And to me, when you think of Kyler Murray, you think really of a lot of scrambling and running that you see in games. And obviously that doesn't happen in these OTAAS. And so what we saw of Kyler was just straight the throwing part of the position. And you could tell there were some times when he was probably bogged down a little bit. You know, the offense for anybody is going to take some time to learn. Um, but you just kept thinking like, I wonder what it would look like if he just took off and ran. And like, and Josh Matelis was talking about that the other day that he's already telling defensive players, be ready for that in training camp because that's an entirely different part of his game that you're not seeing right now. on. So, and I really think that while it's very important for Kyler to be able to throw and and do all the the passing part of this offense, like that scrambling ability is what potentially could be the diff differentiator in this uh competition is just his I mean, he's a 1% scrambler. And so, um, you know, it was great to see him throw, but I'm really looking forward to seeing him run, too. And I would say this as far as JJ McCarthy. Um I mean I I do feel like there has been a level of consistency and accuracy especially when you're thinking like 20 yards and in throughout the five practices that we've been out here. And I I say that because there is a lot of context missing with every one of these practices. And you'd love to see him connect more down the field probably and potentially we'll see that in training camp. But I do think just the fundamentals, the smoothness of his mechanics, that stuff has stood out and his understanding of the system I think stands out. So that was um kind of a layer of this process that does add I would just say another variable as we continue to watch and evaluate it. >> But also the biggest thing is for this offense to succeed is throwing to number 18. Right? Last year it was a struggle and it can't be a struggle. And when Justin rightfully is not doing every single rep out there when it's the seven on sevens because you don't want Justin Jefferson to get banged up in mini camp, it's harder to tell which one of these quarterbacks you'd be leaning toward because the chemistry with Justin Jefferson is going to be a massive factor. And for Kyler Murray and Justin or and uh JJ McCarthy, they're going to get together with Justin through the offseason. And that's going to be a fascinating point when we get to training camp. But as of right now, you know, there were some throws where we saw guys that weren't quite out of their breaks yet, and it got there a little bit early with Kyler cuz he's still feeling that out. So, how quickly can he adapt to a very unique wide receiver in Justin Jefferson? >> It's It's so interesting the way that you're talking about it. It's like we don't really have all the information there yet, but we can tell there's a competition, and that's exactly what Kevin Oonnell said he wanted this entire off season. >> It's also our way of being able to tell people when they ask us who's winning the competition. We don't know. we don't see all all the information. So, it's convenient. >> I will say too, like the first day, I mean, there was no mistaking Kyler Murray's arm and the arm talent and what he could. So, you know, you see certain snippets, certain snapshots of it. And um yeah, the easy thing probably just be settle on one and that's how it goes. But looks like we'll wait. >> But as of right now, why would it benefit them to name a quarterback? I mean, if we go through Vikings history, this is the perfect franchise to say we never know what you're going to get at quarterback position because the discussions we were having during mini camp of 2024 were about, hey, when will Sam Darnold get benched? And the team ends up winning 14 games with him. You know, I was here for the uh Minneapolis Miracle with Case Keenum, which of course everyone saw coming during mini camp. So, if you're Kevin Oonnell, why would you not want to let this thing play out and see how it goes before making a decision right now? >> Yeah. No, most definitely. And while it is the most interesting competition probably on the team right now, I wanted to ask you guys another intriguing position group besides the quarterback that you enjoyed watching during this first, you know, set of offseason programs. And and I'll start with you, Alec. >> Yeah, the offensive line, which probably I would have never thought I would say it. We're proud of you because I don't really I'm not going to pretend like I know everything there. >> You're a big trench guy. >> I Yeah, as a big trench guy myself, having played years of offensive line. No, I I would say um just the level of um intensity I would say with that group every single day. But there have just been a lot of drills, reps, um, practices where you hear those guys, you see them flying off the ball, and then you talk to players like Aaron Jones, TJ Hawinson, they will tell you that there is a different feel from that group and that they believe that's kind of helped set a standard for the whole team. And we'll see come the fall whether that does pay dividends on the field. But to say it looks the same would just not be true. It it has very much looked different. Um, and I'll be curious to see how that translates into training camp. >> Yeah, it's very exciting for this offense. >> To me, what stood out is the receiver group. Um, maybe the the most the deepest uh position on the team. And you think back to last year at the end of training camp when they felt like they needed to trade for Adam Thielen to make sure that they had enough depth just for that week one game. And I think they're way far away from that uh now. I mean, you look at the top three obviously we know they're going to be Jefferson, Addison, and and Jawan Jennings who signed as a free agent. But after that, there's some interesting prospects. I think Miles Price looked pretty good uh in this in this camp. Ty Felton looked much better and and looked like he had a much better feel for how to play at this level. And then they have this Dylan uh Bell, the um undrafted rookie from from Georgia who, you know, I'm not going to pretend to to be able to evaluate him as a great wide receiver mind, but you just see where he's playing and he's with basically the second team and he's catching passes not from Max Bromer and Carson Wentz as much, but from JJ McCarthy or or Ky Kyler Murray and so you take your lead from that and that obviously the coaches um think something of him and want to see how he does in that environment and that was interesting to me. So, they got that's six guys right there. Um, we'll see how many they keep and we'll see what they look like once pads uh are put on in training camp, but that stood out to me by far. For me, it's the safety position because there's this guy, War 22, who is not here right now. And maybe the bat signal goes up and he uh gets off the golf course and shows up here eventually. But as of right now, they're trying to figure out what is life like without Harrison Smith, which it feels like Josh Matelis has sort of been in Harrison Smith training for a couple of years, but hey, he's also played a lot close to the line of scrimmage. So, he talked about moving back away from the football and playing in more of a deep type of role, and that's an adjustment for him that he started to make last year. But, I'm also very intrigued by Jay Ward. We saw a little snippet of Jay Ward get opportunities last year and I was very impressed by his aggressiveness, his tackling. He could come downfield and make plays. He's also a very versatile player. He played a little outside corner, nickel, deep safety. So, where is he going to fit in? And then, you know, you spend a third round draft pick on Jacobe Thomas and what we're hearing already is picking up the defense, high IQ, and I thought that sounds like a Brian Flores safety right there. So, that group is deep and maybe dynamic. So, you're not going to fill in Harrison Smith's shoes, period. But, can you do it with rotating pieces and Josh Mattel is commanding that room? I'll be interested to see how that plays out. >> Yeah, for me it's cornerback. I think that it's really corner corner. Sorry, cornerback. Let's be clear, not cheating. It's actually quarterback. No, it's cornerback right now. I think it's interesting the way that the coaching staff had turned over this off seasonason, bringing in Gerald Alexander, someone that Brian Flores is used to. Um, Funari, who's the assistant coach there, doing a lot of their stats and their presentations and things like that. Shinszo. Yes. Um, I was talking to Isaiah Rogers yesterday, and it just seems like there's a new type of like competition and intensity that comes with a little bit of change and um, and they have a lot of familiarity with themselves, surprisingly, within the group. And then you add someone who I think we're going to get to in just a little bit. Um because I think uh up next for us and what what fans want to get to know is is this team where if I come out to training camp, which you need to go get your tickets right now. Um if you come out here and you're a fan in the stands, Matthew, who is the person that you want to watch? >> Justin Jeff. No, I'm just kidding. Uh >> sorry, we'll say training camp player to watch, right? >> I think fans will know to watch for Justin Jefferson. So I'll go with a deep cut there. fifth round draft pick, Chuck Demings, who I thought, I mean, number one at the combine was one of the most athletic cornerbacks in that, you know, competition. And then when he came out here, you could see it. I mean, you could see the vertical jump from him. You could see the smoothness. You could see the acceleration that he has. And he had several pass breakups where he went very high in the air to make a play on the football. And he comes from Stephen F. Austin, so it's going to be quite the transition from that level to the NFL level. But I think what you're always looking for in that unit is well, who's going to be the next man up? Because we know that, you know, James Pierre and Byron Murphy and Isaiah Rogers have those spots right now, but uh you can never have too many good corners ascending. So I think watching for his athleticism, playmaking ability will be somebody to keep an eye on for the future. >> So very interesting interview as well. >> Yes, for sure. Electric. >> Electric. Yeah, for me it's Dean Claybourne, the the rookie running back and not just because he's from near my hometown in in Virginia, but um over the years just covering mini camps and and OTAAS um here in Minnesota, like there's occasionally a player that you just see has an extra gear from a speed perspective and and this is not to compare him to these players necessarily, but you saw it from Adrien Peterson, you saw it from Percy Harvin. I even thought I saw, you know, Jordan Addison uh that a little bit. And for me seeing that uh over the past week, Devon Claybornne as well returning kicks and also in on offense as well just um you know there's 40 speed and then there's on the field in real time speed and he appears to have both and so we'll see what that looks like in training camp but you know I'm not expecting him to to take over at running back for Aaron Jones or anything but if you have a guy with genuine game speed um as they hope he does have and he displayed uh this week to us there's there's going to be a place for him in offense and and this is not just because everyone's going to be asking me fantasy questions and how should I draft him on Claybornne and and they use them like two plays a game but those two plays could be very impactful and so I I'm really interested to see like how that speed translates when they're in pads and how it maintains and if he can work himself into a position where he's got a roll with the offense from the beginning of the season. >> Do people ask you a lot of fantasy football questions? Yes. >> Oh boy. They think you're >> I shouldn't advert I shouldn't advertise that because now I'll be getting more. But I never answer them right. So and as Bill Parcels has always said the the uh the value of my advice is commensurate with the with the price that I charge. And so there you go. >> Which is zero. And so I wouldn't listen to me if if I were you. >> All right. So we're going two rookie draft picks. >> I'm following up with another. Yeah. Caleb Banks. Um, I mean, really from the outset, it feels like Kevin Oonnell and this Viking staff pinpointed training camp as the time for him to potentially start to ease in back on the field. And it was obviously a major swing of a first round pick and a guy who you can see it as he walked by today at practice. I mean, he is a massive human being and a guy when you watch the tape has a ton of talent and physical attributes that you just don't see all the time. And so, um, first to see him healthy, second to see what he looks like in this system working with Ryan Nielsen, the new defensive line coach who will will demand a certain standard every day. Um, and then just what it looks like collectively, him alongside Andrew Van Ginkle, Dallas Turner, that um, is fascinating for me to just consider and to think about. So, he's the obvious, probably most lowhanging fruit answer, but can't wait to just see what he looks like out there. >> Yeah, should be a really fun time. Training camp is going to be a lot of fun. But I'm going to change tunes a little bit here because we haven't really gotten to speak to you guys or talk to you guys since the Vikings announced Nolan Teasley as their new general manager. title: Saints QB Tyler Shough on offseason training, connecting with Drew Brees, leadership, Erik McCoy
text: Tell her, what is this I don't even think you got any starts with him under your belt last year, but having Eric just slide back in the mix healthy, like what does he do for you guys offensively? >> I mean, I think he just adds that extra veteran element where he's seen a lot of football. He's been great for me. Him and I, even though we didn't get to play together, we were around each other every single day going to O-line dinners and I mean, we had our son born within a 24 hours of each other. So, we were at the hospital together and you know, I love him. So, he's been great for me just to be able to learn and talk with him. Um, I think they for the whole O-line group, I think it's kind of just solidified our position. >> Yeah, especially for a guy, I mean, this is like going to be I think year nine for him, year eight, something like that. I mean, that I mean, that's got to help you just being a young guy. >> Yeah, no doubt. I mean, there's a trust element for sure. When whatever he's calling, unless there's something drastic that I can override, I trust him fully and implicitly and it makes a lot of fun, too, when we're all on the same page. >> Tell her, how have you and him been doing in practice if you don't mind? Is he texting you a lot? Do a lot of stories and he's like texting you a lot? >> Yeah, we were texting all throughout the off season. I don't know who was texting who. He was sending me sending me some stuff in all of his his Derby days and all the things that he was doing. And I I could tell just he wants to be here. He understands this is his place, this is his home and he's been such a great leader and influence for me being from the same hometown, who he is as a person, his impact on the community and I can't be more happy to have him back cuz he just brings that element >> Tyler, how's the off season training been so far for you too this off season? >> The off season what? >> Training. Training, yeah. >> Uh, I mean, it's been it's been amazing. I've been able to put on 6 lbs of muscle, been able to drop my body fat. You're getting a whole off season underneath your belt and I just feel feel comfortable. You know, obviously there's there's new things every single day from a mental perspective, but it's it's more review and and how can we kind of get on the same page with all these new guys, you know. That's going to be the challenge going into the training camp is that sense of urgency with with Olave, [snorts] with Tyson, with Valdes-Scantling, with Polk, and all of our guys and how can we just kind of take it to the next level. >> Even though Jordan's been kind of sidelined most of the time, how have you guys built up chemistry so far? >> Yeah, I mean we're hanging out probably every other day. You know, he's a young 21-year-old. I remember being being the same age few years back and just we're hanging out, watching, you know, movies. We're watching the NBA finals together. We're coming over having food together. He's he's such a great guy. Being able to just whether it's getting jobs, going through the walk-throughs together. So, I mean he's jumped in even in these walk-throughs and he's hasn't messed up, you know, missed a play or missed a beat. He's super smart. And obviously he's he's I mean he's ready to go. He's going to be he's going to be firing on all cylinders. So, I can't wait to to get going with him. >> All right. We got to have more than that. What is So, what's next up for you this off-season? I mean you got I mean you got a six-week break pretty much. What do you want to work on? >> Yeah, I'll be in Oregon and then I'll be in San Diego. We're just going to help in setting up our you know, our QB room and we're throwing the tree. So, we're getting all the guys to come down there and being able to just work and and bond together and then for me it's just kind of continuing to to study the playbook and then just put my feet and my eyes in the right position. You know, that's my whole focus and right now, you know, this OTA phase, you know, you're not necessarily getting full speed padded reps, but you know, you're installing all these new plays, making sure we're getting everything right. I think we've done a really good job of that as a team. And we've gotten closer. That's kind of the main thing. We just highlighted in the team meeting room all the fun things that we've done this whole off-season and this is probably the the tightest bunch that all of us have been around. >> Talking about your personality. That's the thing that's showing up the most here since I traded this year. What is examples of that of your personality that >> Yeah, I mean who I am in media is is not who I am. I'm not ever like that every single day in the locker room. You know, I'm I'm interacting with all the guys. I like to have fun. I'm super outgoing. Um I think it's This is a tough business. There's a lot of scrutiny and there's a lot of day-to-day elements of it. There's a It's a long season. You have to have fun coming into work here. Cuz it's all in God's hands anyways and it's everything that we're doing was It's for his glory. It's for you know, this purpose of we're trying to get better. Um so I think that's the biggest thing is that we've all bonded. We've all had a lot of fun and Joan's been the big influence of that for sure. >> Taylor, just to get all the slot receivers and see how they fit in. >> So far. >> How challenging has it been so far getting the backs >> I don't know how challenging has it been so far getting the backs and the new receivers? >> Yeah, I mean it's an ongoing process. I don't think it's been challenging per se just because they're they do such a great job of of studying and and you just understanding you know, how they move and how they move on the field but that just comes with time. Um but they've done a great job of it. We're going to continue to do that. >> Taylor, with you and coach Lonnie and some of the coaches being here for us going into year two now, how has that continuity helped the team this off season? >> I think it's I think it's everything. I think being able to sit down and review previous film instead of you know, years past or you you can evaluate yourself. You know, maybe we change this footwork on this play or maybe we add an element on this play that we hadn't had before. Um so it makes it a lot more engaging that way and then also I also know some of the things I can continue to work on. You know, I've only played half a season and you know, I have a long way to go when it comes to development wise and and I'm really excited to kind of keep going. >> Do you think your confidence in yourself as a quarterback in this league has increased a bit this off stuff in the air more this off season? >> Yeah, no doubt. I think it's all It comes down to my preparation, my routine, knowing that there's going to be ups and downs and how to like stick to it and be the same person every single day. That's my whole goal and you know, I'm going to do everything I can do to make us make us better. >> This might be a dumb question but you guys spent a lot of time in shotgun last year. So it's like 75% of the snaps. Was that maybe something that that was related to like your comfort? Like are you more comfortable in shotgun or under center? Does it really matter to you? Like would that be something that y'all could be more of this year than under center? >> Yeah, I think I'm comfortable with both. I feel like we've done a good job of of utilizing both. I think there's going to be elements of that and you know, that's what you're going to see on the film this year. It's us going under center, you know, using shotgun and I think that's the whole goal is to be balanced. >> Tyler, probably not very common that a guy plays at three colleges and ends up with teammates in the NFL from all three schools. But all seriousness, does that kind of make you like a bit of a chameleon in the locker room having so many different experiences, being able to manage different personalities? >> Yeah, I think you know, I've been able to learn over time just to be yourself and and in order to be a a good leader, you have to serve others and you have to develop those relationships and and at times I wasn't in the past and at times you you know, you're going to have bad games, you're going to have a bad throw. How do you respond to it and how do you respond when others have a bad day and it's part of it and being able to experience that through those years in college is is everything and you know, Zach and I talk about it all the time being from the same class and and what he's been able to to learn from this point in the league we're both kind of you know, I think really at peace mentally about our own journey and how can we can kind of continue to get better. >> Any fun plans? >> Um Going to I mean, the main thing is San Diego. I think going to there to to work out with the guys, going to the beach. I'll stay here in in New Orleans this whole off season at this point. So, it'll be it'll be nice to um to get out of the heat for a little bit, but still come right back to it and I think that's the main thing is is not going too far and then I'll be back a couple weeks early before camp. So, to work with the guys. So >> When you meet the guys, play volleyball with you? >> No, I don't know. It's not going to be Top Gun or anything like that. I think we might play golf a little bit out there, but a lot of a lot of it's going to be working out, throwing, having the guys over the house, getting the pool, stuff like that. >> But you are big intramural, right? I think you posted about >> Yeah, yeah, I was a shout out uh Seager's Sandbar White Sands. Man, there's a I'm a big beach volleyball guy. I I've definitely learned I have a lot more respect for those guys cuz I I did it after like a 2-hour practice and then we had a whole tournament and I couldn't even walk the next day. It was It was insane, so it should be fun.

title: Saints TE Noah Fant on working with Tyler Shough, getting acclimated to New Orleans
text: He's running the offense really well, so he's doing everything that he needs to be doing and we got to, you know, support him and and be where we where he needs to speak. >> For you just your adjusting here, how how is that going for you and do you feel like you're kind of settling in? >> Like the city? >> City, personally, yeah. >> Yeah, no, it's been great. I I've never lived in the South before. So, I was a little nervous at first, but it's been great, man. It's great food, great culture, great people.
