title: Saints HC Kellen Moore on re-signing Cam Jordan, teaching rookies the playbook, final minicamp day
text: All right. So, day two of mini camp here will be outside weather permitting. We should look good. A little bit of a red zone emphasis today, some two-minute introductions, and should be in a good place. A couple roster updates, additions that we're signing. Jaylon Moreno-Cropper, receiver. Uh he was with the Cowboys. He was in the UFL. He played Fresno State. Hunter Dekkers, quarterback, was in the UFL. Obviously, we had Hunter last year. And then Tanner Brown, kicker. He was in the UFL with the King, the Kings. He played Oki State. So, we signed him. We had And then obviously Cam Jordan, not to be forgotten. >> [laughter] >> But >> What UFL team was he >> He was not, but it was >> It was fun introducing Cam in front of the team like he was an addition to the roster. It was kind of a, you know, fun one this year introducing guys. And we had a few releases as result of that cuz I Cosiah was released. DeShawn Jones, Mason Shipley, and Damien Alford will be waved injured. So, I'll open up to questions. >> When did Damien get hurt? >> Uh last week. >> Getting the Cam thing done, >> [snorts] >> what does that mean to you? >> Yeah, excitement. Um obviously, um you know, guys in his situation have to go through a process during the offseasons to to make decisions that are best for them. And obviously, we feel fortunate and excited that it um you know, the opportunity presented itself and it was the right alignment as far as getting him back and um you know, I'm I'm excited. >> He said that the his teammates, past and current, were pinging on him a lot in the last few months. He mentioned you doing that, too. How much does that mean to you that the seems like the whole team wanted him back, too? I mean, that matters, right? >> Yeah, I think that's an important thing you know, when you're building the program, culture, environment, uh you want to build the build it around the right kind of guys. And Uh, when these guys are bought in collectively, I think that's a sign of the right kind of guys and uh Cam did an excellent job, you know, from my experience just being with him last year, his his experience and veteran leadership through a season that we had to navigate some things early on. He did an excellent job through that and so, excited to get him back into this thing and get him acclimated and ready to go. >> Kellen, did you expect Cam to pretty much with coach Daly as far as playing time get the same numbers of snaps? You know, he was playing a lot with Chase Young, but uh, not like he was earlier on his career. It was like 90% of the time, but around 45% of the snaps in that rotation or >> Yeah, I think he'll definitely be part of that rotation. I think to our advantage as a football team, we have added some depth in that group. That's going to be a benefit for us and so, what those numbers look like, you know, hey, they're all going to contribute. They're all going to contribute and that's an important aspect to this thing and because of the versatility of these guys, I think you're going to be able to utilize more than just two of them at times when you want to in some third down situations, which is a positive thing for us and Cam will continue to you know, carry a very valuable role with that. >> Cam mentioned that you called him a few times, told him that you wanted to respect his space, but when you're coming in, can you tell us a little bit about your your end of those conversations and what those conversations >> my goal always is just to be a resource for guys in Cam's situation. Again, he's got to make the decision that's best for him. Obviously, he knows how we feel, but I also want to be a resource to answer questions and you know, help him navigate what this situation looks like for him and so, yeah, I think what was awesome about Cam and our organization was just the healthy conversations that went on and certainly Mickey and Cam had a number of those and so, you know, I think everything's in a good space. >> How often would you estimate you and him talked over the course of that process? >> Mainly just one time. You know, business side of it, they kind of had to navigate early on and then just being a resource. >> With Eric [clears throat] McCoy, I was wondering, you know, you obviously before taking this job looked at the 2024 film. You saw the difference between him not being there and out. I guess like when he was injured for you last year, like did you notice a difference or like was it like, "Wow, this is actually really hard to replace this guy?" Like how what kind of went through your mind as a coach when you have to replace someone of that caliber? >> Eric's one of the top centers in this league. He's a really talented player. When he's on the field, we're a better football team always. Last year we were fortunate that we were able to have Luke available to us and so that really kind of you know, saved us in many ways from having to do a big you know, shuffling of the deck and so you know, that was a positive experience for us because of that, but you know, Eric's still an important part of this. So you know, when he's out there, we're a better offensive line, we're a better offense and so excited to keep building. >> Kellen, have you ever been a part of a Like I know teams have played practice against two teams in the preseason, but now going against three against Jacksonville, the Rams and and Dallas. >> Not three, we've done two at a few other spots. Um what's happened in the past sometimes is we do two days with with a team. You know, I I was in LA when the Saints came out to California and we were with the Chargers and we did two days. And so a lot of times you ended up with four total joint practice days accounted for there and so essentially doing one day with three teams, you get three practices and be great work. >> Kellen, last year I think the 11-on-11 drills were kind of saved for training camp. This year you've done a lot more of them. What's the reason for the kind of increase in these drills? >> I think part of it is getting yourself acclimated for what you're going to be asked to do in training camp. So you know, really OTAs is a build into training camp and so we kind of talked about you know, we have to learn how to walk through the right way. We We to learn how to practice the right way and then eventually we have to learn how to operate in a team setting. Um And protect our self as teammates as we kind of go through that. And so I think that was an important part as we kind of continue to build this thing. And so early was installation, a lot of more jog through settings as you guys saw in the, you know, post practice or the late part of practice. And you know, we just kind of kept stacking and so the last few days we've been able to incorporate more of the team stuff and pre-snap penalties we got to be cleaner. We got to get ready to practice because we're not practice that way a whole lot and get the team involved cuz the O-line D-line, you know, they kind of without that team component they're essentially an individual most of the day. >> What makes Anthony Richardson like special or different against, you know, defending the run? >> [clears throat] >> Yeah, I think obviously strength, stoutness, physical play. I think he's got a really high IQ. You can tell he he just processes the game in a very easy manner. I think what's cool is watching him just hop in there and try and find every opportunity he can to help this team, you know, I think the special teams component is kind of cool. Talked about that with Tyree yesterday. These guys are just trying to find roles and find opportunities which is great. And you know, he's played a whole bunch of games for a reason because he's a really consistent physical football player. >> Kellen, when you go into like a up tempo or no huddle is it like a game plan at times where a particular opponent, okay, we think we can utilize this to our advantage or is it like a game time, okay, we got to get something going, uh, light a spark, whatever. We going no huddle to attack them. What approach do you take on >> Yeah, tempo can come in a lot of different reasons. Obviously you can focus on yourself and try and get the juice, get the energy going. I think a lot of times um guys play really clean football. A lot of these guys come from college where they're used to being in no huddle. The huddle setting is actually kind of foreign to them. As funny as that sounds. And then when you play an opponent, there's obviously advantage to that. You know, it's harder for them to substitute. You can kind of identify what they're in. It's harder to disguise. You know, some teams do an excellent job disguising, and you're trying to get on the ball to kind of avoid some of those challenges, and so um there's a lot of different reasons, but there's a flow to the game of when to do it and when not to do it, and you know, it's a it's an important part of our system. >> To clarify on the 11s question that Jeff asked, like when you look back at your first year, was it felt like maybe something in retrospect you needed to do more of your first season, or was it just this is where our group is at now? >> I Yeah, it has more to do with this being year two, flow operation, uh a ton of installation last off season with a new staff obviously, and everyone teaming together. And so this year I felt like we're in a much better place and ready to get into an 11-on-11 setting. >> With the with the huddle thing, like just kind of how they operate in college, are there things you do that kind of cater to like how they're coming up now that maybe would be against like your ideal way just because it's not worth fighting it, or it's just the way the game's played now? >> Yeah, I think it's there's definitely some awareness to it. Um the way you call plays, the way you operate, um there's a way that we've all been accustomed to, and there's a way that these guys have kind of trained theirself that's different. A lot of them see it more in a conceptual world, so one thing that happens a lot more in college is yes, there's no huddle. Uh there's much more non-verbal uh communication, and then the play calls are much shorter. A lot of times they view it as one word means the whole picture, you know, so you can say apple, making something up, and everyone knows what apple is across the entire thing, where we're more accustomed to tagging everything out and explaining it in a longer form. These guys are much more visual, so our sequence is teaching this thing from a wider lens, you know, explaining kind of of of it. And then as we kind of build into training camp and into the season, the play calls usually naturally get a little bit shorter, a little bit tighter, and that's where these guys are more accustomed to, anyways. >> How do you go about moving them from I mean, you say visual, I think about the cards on the sideline, the signal cards, and and things of that. How do you go about moving players from that to the verbal communication? >> Yeah, I think it's a great experience for these guys. Um you know, and and they've all been exposed. I mean, it's not like, you know, it's all bad or anything like that. I think it's just a different way that they visualize the game. And so, it's just an education opportunity for us. Again, um you know, we also have a responsibility to meet them a little bit where they're at, and so, uh we'll bring them along the way along the way. And so, uh you know, for these younger guys, we kind of keep them usually in one form one position more often early, and then we'll expand their roles as they go. >> Ron, what was it about Spencer that you wanted to keep around after, you know, losing the starting job, and just like, you know, still develop him as a as a young quarterback? >> Spencer's young. He's a really talented quarterback. I think the world of the guy. Uh I thought he played good football last year. Um I think we're fortunate to still have him have him here, and we get to continue to develop him, and you know, I think we have a really talented quarterback room. >> Yesterday, uh Cam said that he thinks Chase Young's capable of having like a 20-sack season. Do you see, you know, a ceiling for him to to be something high like that? And what is it about him that makes you think like this guy could, you know, have like such a special season like that? >> Yeah, feel great about Chase. Feel like uh he's gotten better from my exposure being with him for the last year and a half now. Just the growth he's taken, and the I guess just the preparation, the work ethic that he's shown uh through the off-season is really impressive. Like, this guy loves to work. He loves to work really hard. Um I think he's gotten better. You can see as the season went on, he just kept getting better, and I think this off-season has been a good indication of where he's going. Uh the leadership that he's provided, the energy he provides certainly. Uh, but he's just, you know, he's looking like he's getting better each and every day. >> And how much about like Brandon's scheme do you think plays a role in that for that front? >> Yeah, I think there's a benefit to that. Uh, you know, obviously I think what Brandon's experienced and you look at his track record with the edge rushers at all the different spots that they've been, Chicago, Denver, LA, LA, um, now here. Um, you know, I think they do an excellent job, him and Jay do an excellent job of teaming up coaching these edges and providing them with a bunch of tools, but also enough uh, flexibility to go go let it go and let it loose and uh, you know, be able to attack off the edge. >> Beyond the football part with Chase Young, do you see a difference in him just in his attitude, his just the the he he he seems more, I don't know, what's the word, more open, more freer, just in in >> Yeah. >> Do you Do you see that? >> I think that's a fair assessment. Uh, you know, I think when you have a successful season and you kind of are building, confidence comes from that and I think you can sense that from uh, from Chase and I think also also when Cam wasn't around, there's an expectation of, you know, there's a leadership void there and you know, for Chase, for Grando, for uh, Chris Rumph, you know, these guys who've kind of been here to help lead that group, I think is an important part. >> He was someone too that you guys like placed a lot of pretty high expectations on in terms of just like talking to us like we can work with Chase and like play, you know, um, I'm just wondering like when you set those expectations, he delivers on them, what does that do for you guys as a group? >> Yeah, I [clears throat] I think we all feel really confident about Chase and he had to navigate the injury early in the year where he wasn't able to play and that was frustrating for him just because, you know, you're trying to get ready to go and uh, you have to navigate that. But once he got on the field, I thought his effort and his play styles is a perfect example of how we want to play and so we want that to show up each and every day. >> You mentioned >> the impact that Luke had last year and you mentioned Tyree, Jaylen, Davante. Like, you've made several trades for these maybe I guess buy low, taking swings at young rookie contract guys. Is that a philosophy you've always supported or did you see it work in an instance and then kind of drift to that? Just what's the thought behind some of those >> Yeah, I I guess yeah, that's that's a good one. Um other places I'm sure we've had different exposures that have been successful. I thought last year, um you know, including Tyree now this year I think just a really good job of our personnel department with Mickey uh just continue to explore every avenue and uh you know, I think you can see what Jaylen Polk's example is is having a full season to be here and how he's just jumped right into it because he's been around for a long time and I think that was a really creative way of adding depth to our receiver room and viewing it beyond just a 6-month perspective. You know, a lot of times we can be very focused in the here and now but you have to blend that with where you're going and so um you know, I think we've done some really good moves like that. >> Kelvin, when you look at the running game, do you think uh you know, obviously we need a shotgun, the RPOs and the ability of quarterback being able to run that's a big, big plus in the running game. But do you think from the shotgun, will it ever catch up to being under the center to truly smashmouth run the football and and being able to average on say 4.3 yards a carry uh and just how how dangerous all that is because you don't want to get the quarterback hurt and just but just handing off the ball in the shotgun it's not like being under the center as far as >> I mean, coming off the ball and and winning in in that regard. >> Yeah, I think that's a fair assessment. I think it's it starts with matching your scheme to your players and what best suits them. I think the second part is creating mastery and kind of uh not being a a jack of all master none. I think we're trying to do a better job of that this year as far as, you know, keeping this thing really clean and defined and get us get really good reps at certain things and so history of our league's gone up and down, you know. Philly had a bunch of top running games where they're all living in the shotgun. A couple other teams have certainly the under center run games. I think getting a little bit trendy again now. It's kind of con come back full circle with, you know, the LAs and some of those teams of the world getting back under center and so I think we followed that trend a little bit as the back end of the year went where um you can run the football under center a little bit better. You have to be conscious of the quarterback run game. Um you know, those are potential hits on your quarterbacks so you have to be smart about that and so um we're just continuing to evolve. >> Let's take two more. >> What is Bob means dealing with currently? >> Yeah, he just had a he just had a little lower body injury so he's just coming back. Again, for all these guys we're just if you have a little bit of an injury this time of year, our goal is to shoot you up and get you ready for training camp. So just build you back up and then um so that when we leave like we leave tomorrow or today actually tomorrow we won't have practice and um we just want these guys to have a really good cuz they can take advantage of these next five and a half weeks before training camp and that's an important part for us. >> Will any of the wrap-up guys do anything more today like Alvin in team drills or anything like that? >> No, I think it'll look it'll look the same as what it was yesterday.

title: Emeka Egbuka, Antoine Winfield Jr. & More on Team's Energy | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: What's up, y'all? Good. Yeah, yeah. Those are some big shoes to fill right there. But, um it's been great. I've just been enjoying the process of my role and my position on the team. And obviously, without those guys, other people need to step up, including myself. And so, you know, I'm just going to honor that role and just do the best that I can. Yeah, for sure, for sure. Whenever you can make plays, I think that gets everybody excited. >> Antoine, with so many new faces in front of you on defense, how much if it's what you guys want it to be, how much can that change the entire defense, especially on the back end? >> It'll help a lot. You know, the game starts up front. So, if you have a dominant front seven, it makes everybody's job way easier. And if they can control the game, then we'll we'll be better off this this season. >> Antoine, what have you seen from Tykee Smith in terms of the leadership role? He's kind of biding his time a little bit. >> Yeah. >> A guy that's been pretty vocal in practice that you've been catching to. >> Yeah, a guy that's stepping up, filling that role. You know, he's helping out a lot that in that aspect. But, great player. He's been improving every single year and he's had some great years in the past and he's just he's one of those guys that's that's stepping up. >> Antoine, the the middle of the defense, the secondary last year was an issue. You got a couple new linebackers in front of you. How does that help? How does that all come together? >> It's coming together great so far. You know, we're taking steps each and every day, but we got some we got some great great players filling in. Vass, Alex, those guys have been doing great. So, it'll be a fun year with those guys. >> We've heard of tweaking of the scheme in the secondary. Can you talk a little bit about that and in your mind? >> Yeah, we got some new stuff in. Um I don't know if I can share too much, but uh it's been nice. >> You spoke about Alex Anzalone. You competed against him for years with the Lions and all that, but but what has he brought from the leadership standpoint and just also like a size, play-making standpoint as >> a guy that can really cover. >> Yeah, I would say he brought in that veteran presence. Um you know, and as far as the linebacker room, you know, he's a vet he's been playing um for a while at a at a high level. So, having him come in and and fill one of those roles, you know, it's great to have him out there and being able to, you know, do everything. >> It's pretty early on in camp, but with the install and all that, but what are your first thoughts on Zach Robinson's offense that you're playing against at the moment in the Lions? Yeah, no, he has he has some nice stuff. I'm not going to lie. I see some plays I'm like, "Okay, that's nice. That that should work during the season." So, it's been uh great going up against it cuz it you know gives us some work as well, gives us some different looks that we're going to see when we go against other teams. So, it's been nice kind of battling with each other. >> And then last year you guys had to dedicate so many resources to stop him. >> And and that the better or worse left you kind of playing some center field maybe more than you did want to. >> You know you can get involved at all three levels. Um are you hopeful this year that, you know, with with some of the new guys up front you can bring that that old game back and and and not be the literal safety that has to kind of keep the top on, you know. >> Yeah, yeah, for sure, very hopeful. Very hopeful. You know, my my best skill set I feel like is my versatility. So, being able to play everywhere is what I like the most. So, I think that'll definitely help with that. >> You've kind of become a model of second generation NFL players that have found success early on and sustained it. Um you have a a young teammate in Josh Paschal following in those footsteps. What kind of advice would you give him as he transitions to this next level with a lot of expectations? >> Yeah, um I would say the first thing, don't be too hard on yourself. You know, play at your own pace, um work at your own pace. You know, you got to set those goals for yourself coming in and you can say that to any one of the rookies that come in each and every year. It's a a mentality thing. You know, everybody's big, everybody's fast, everybody's strong, and everybody has a different approach, but you want to come in with the the right mindset that you're going to get better every day and that you're coming out here to be the best. >> What about you and your dad as far as how you navigated it? Because I know early on you would do like the you know, sometimes like the twice weekly watching the film >> I don't know if that's a thing anymore, but but as you've gotten older, you know, we we see less and less of him and and even when you got your new contract and things like that, like how how did you kind of you guys kind of navigate >> Yeah, um you know, obviously I got some years under my belt now. So, um I'm feeling pretty confident in in in the way I study and what I do and I've been prepared, you know, I've been preparing my entire life for it and so I feel like at this point in my career uh I think I got a good good hold of everything that I need to do. >> And he's I was going to say he's still just as big of a fan of yours. >> 100% 100%. >> Antoine, you talk about the oldest receiver, Chris Godwin, the off season he's had and how he's looked and also or the younger guys, said Hurst and what you what your impressions are of the third round draft pick. >> Yeah, yeah, he's been making some crazy catches. I'm not going to lie. Um big body, big frame, um he can he has great ball skills, so he's he's going to be nice for us this year. >> And Chris Godwin? >> Chris Chris is still the same Chris. Um you know, he you know, he struggled with some injuries last season and the previous season, but um he's been improving and getting better and back to himself 100%. >> Antoine, do you feed off some of that chirping that's going on with the defensive lineman? You got Robinson and he likes to talk and you got there's like Nacho who you know how that is. >> yeah. >> Do you feed off that kind of stuff? >> Yeah, yeah. It's fun. It's uh it's great to hear. You know, you love to see it out of the guys and you want to play with guys that are chirping a little bit, you know, it builds that, you know, intensity and you know, we just kind of follow suit with that. This team's probably going to finish somewhere in the middle of the pack again. Last year wasn't a deep quarterback class and neither was 2025. >> Mhm. >> Um you know, what it's got to be a deep quarterback class at the top. If you can have four or five guys, the Steelers can go up and nab the fourth guy, but they probably aren't getting the top two. And so that's always the big thing with the and the big hurdle is there's so many quarterback needy teams in the NFL from year to year that it's just hard to get them. So, you got to make a move up the board to really stamp uh your mark on that. And so, have the Steelers taken it seriously? Probably not, but they also have kind of said, "We're not just going to spend draft capital just to spend it. We're not just going to draft a quarterback because we need a quarterback. If we don't believe in that quarterback, why are we taking that guy?" And I do think there's something to be said about that. If you don't believe in a guy like that, don't take Don't they believe in Kenny Pickett, but they passed on very similar players to him before that have been in in somewhat of a an area, maybe better prospects, I you know, a Dart or a a Simpson. Are they better prospects than Pickett? They're probably on a similar plane. Um but like they don't believe in them like that, it's very hard to argue they should take them. So, there's a real kind of take and give. But, this is why I think the topic of should the Steelers just not try and win one year is such a big topic. It is The idea is you will tank one year to get down to the point where you can get a quarterback, but the Steelers don't want to do that. Um we have seen at times there are teams that totally tear it down to the studs and rebuild it and it works. Other times you end up like the New York Jets where it's just perpetual losing. You never get out of the hole, right? So, there's a risk to it. Um >> [snorts] >> and so, there's a lot of processes to it. And there's also examples of teams like the Steelers, you know, that have done it before. Uh Kansas City traded up, you know, 17, 18 spots to go get Patrick Mahomes. Buffalo was I think uh around 18th that year when they got Josh Allen. Um we've seen teams do that before where they've taken a guy and traded up and gotten them. Um and so, I I what the Steelers need to do or they need a veteran to become available and they need to take a swing on that veteran. I mean that's the other way they could do this, right? You get a Matthew Stafford on the trade market, you get a Jared Goff on the trade market, someone like that. Um we haven't really seen a lot of veteran trades on the quarterback market recently that have been at that level, but that's the other way the Steelers could maybe crack it. Is if, you know, someone in that tier became available, but um they really kind of just have to wait and see for the right quarterback class. They wanted a quarterback last year. They set it up. We talked about this. The compensatory pick formula that they had set up completely so they could trade up and still address all their needs. Um they set up for that last year, but that quarterback class really cratered. Um and so you'd hope this year is stronger again, but you really don't know until you get, you know, November, December what you're dealing with. >> No, you you you were spot-on, Nick. This dual mandate coming down from Art Rooney himself of keep winning, contend for the playoffs every year, but also, hey, yeah, let's uh find and develop our franchise guy. Those are at loggerheads with each other. But I do think the model is there that even if you are drafting, you know, down around 20, which the Steelers have done a lot of, 20, 21, whatever whatever those slots are, if you have the guy you fall in love with, like you said, doing your due diligence and falling in love with the tools and the character, you go ahead and you trade up to get those guys like the Mahomes, you know, uh and like the Josh Allens. That's the model. That's the model. You got to fall in love, uh do your due diligence, make sure he is the guy, and then take your swing and do it that way. That's the way you got to do it. Um because I I agree that there is a trap uh for tanking and losing. That's That's not a good signal to send and and I I think you can get trapped down there in in that loser mentality. You know, like you mentioned the Jets. I think there's something I think there's something to that. It's not that easy to turn it on and off. I think the Rams successfully did it, you know, rebooted. I think the next day. So like that could happen. But are they going to go into week one with four quarterbacks? I doubt it. I I just It's not It's not good roster building. I think they like all four of them, but this is going to be a competition between Rudolph and Howard. That is what it is. I don't understand the roster building argument to keep four quarterbacks. You know what I mean? Uh Mason Rudolph has been there, done that. We know what he is. And he's fine backup, but but will Howard, you know, I just think you know, that he has youth on his side and he has maybe not the highest ceiling in the land, but but he does have some upside there and you know, I just think that that that's something you can't deny. >> As long as he has a high enough floor this year to where they can comfortably just say, all right, if we put you in, the the ball ball's not going to fall out on this team. >> Right. >> he is going to be the guy you know, they'd prefer. It's just going to be you know, if he's a disaster. I mean, they they He's a sixth round pick. I keep saying it. >> Oh, yeah. >> They're not holding to him. Um, you know, so if he is just a disaster, they're not just going to keep him cuz he's young. But you know, I I've seen him play in minicamp this year. I think he looks fine. I think he looks solid. We've talked about him being a high floor player. I think he is that. I think he's a guy that probably makes this roster. It's kind of where I would go with it right now if I were doing a projection and Rudolph would be traded, you know, something like that. But there's no doubt about it in my mind. The battle's between those two. So, that's going to be the QB2 job in the battle for those two. Uh, but Allen's not going anywhere, obviously. Rodgers is a lock. So, one of those two has to has to be moved. Um, and I think the Steelers, as we've talked about, would prefer that to be Will Howard, but he's going to have to prove it first. >> And another thing about Howard, you have noted his accuracy in what you've seen so far in the, you know, mini camp and OTAs, which is which is, you know, accuracy in delivery, you know, the football is has been looking good for Howard. There's still a lot of things that to work on. He doesn't have the strongest arm of these of this crew. Um, that's certainly something that'll be a a big thing. The footwork for him has to stay consistent. That was a big issue of his coming out of Ohio State and how he deals with pressure's going to be big, but also I could point to Mason Rudolph and say that's a lot of his issues, too. Um, so, um, how how much of a floor raiser is Mason Rudolph? I think you know what he is, um, but if Will Howard has more and more upside and is really knocking on the door and is maybe even just a little bit worse than Rudolph or even, you know, even, uh, you got to go with the young guy. >> Oh, absolutely. No no-brainer there. Another intriguingly crowded room for the Steelers that's going to be sorted out in training camp and the preseason is that RB room. And, uh, we have Vince Williams, you know, ex-linebacker proclaiming, "I don't think we're going to miss our MVP that much." He's referring to Kenny Gainwell, who last year hauled in 73 passes in addition to, you know, uh, his gains on the ground, uh, and was a nice, uh, chemistry with, uh, Aaron Rodgers. Uh, he has departed for greener pastures and green money. Duddle bring a lot of different things that Kenny Gainwell didn't bring. You know, Duddle's more of a hammer between the tackles and you're going to see Jaylen Warren work more into the Gainwell role where he's going to be the guy out in space. And in terms of tackle breaking efficiency, Jaylen Warren's always been one of the better running backs in the NFL. That's been his superpower. So, I do think there's some merit to it. I do think, you know, you look at Duddle at times, he can become a bit of a plodder. And he kind of needs volume to get going. It's like an engine heating up, like you kind of need to give him time to get going. He kind of gets better as the game goes on cuz he's just such a big guy. He's going to wear you down. I think with Warren in the fold and the way he runs behind his pads and how violent he is, you'll really be able to see this duo kind of work well. I do think they're going to miss Gainwell's pass pro. I think that's really where I look at. You know, Duddle's not quite the pass pro and receiver that Gainwell was. Gainwell was a three-down running back much like Warren is a three-down running back. To me, you look at Dowdle, he's more of like a two-down running back. Can he do third down, fourth down stuff? Um We talk about a guy like that, he is the sleeper of this room that I hope people keep their eyes on. I've talked about him a few times in videos on this uh platform. He's your ideal kind of running back three-four type that if Morin got hurt, he could take the kind of dirty stuff and allow Dowdle to just take the mantle as kind of the runner, but on third downs, if you needed a guy to come in, Homer could do that. Uh Highn Right can play a lot of different spots. Caleb Johnson is trying to diversify his game. I think that running back three spots going to be a really fun battle to watch. Who's going to win it? I think it's going to be really really kind of interesting cuz are they going to keep three or four running backs? I think it's still a question up in the air, but I think two of those running backs have a ton of special teams uh and receiving versatility. I think KJ is kind of the potential, right? He's kind of the potential guy um that you're looking at. You're like, what's KJ going to be like uh this year? Um but I also think you do look at what Gainwell brought, and there is some concern there that, you know, are they going to lose some of the the yak ability he had on space and some of the ability he had to be a three-down interchangeable running back cuz I don't totally think Dowdle is a true pure four-down running back like Gainwell was. >> Uh I think you're right, and yeah, I think it's uh too easy to just sort of wave goodbye and say, "Hey, we're we're we've replaced everything that Gainwell uh Gainwell gave us last year. So uh that remains to be seen but great analysis of that whole room and and the coming you know, get your popcorn out and watch watch those battles in training camp. That that'll be fun. You know, there's these sort of uh um uh exploratory articles and things you hear but is there anything in reality of how this uh three-way edge monster is going to play out this season and in the coming year 2027. >> Yeah. I mean nothing really new from what we talked about last week. I I think you think about that. They're going to find creative ways to get them on the field. I think they're going to up Herbig's snap count, try to keep Watt fresh, try to keep Highsmith healthy. Um and that's kind of how I see it. I mean, Herbig's going to be the guy over the middle, I think, more so. He'll play A gap, B gap, outside. He can play off the ball more than the other two probably can. And that's kind of his superpower. He opens up a lot of what they can do schematically up the middle and with their blitz packages. So, I think he's going to play more, especially with the sub package world they're going to really, really dive into with Patrick Graham's defense. They played a lot of sub package stuff, obviously, last year, but I think Patrick Graham's even going to amplify that more. I think that amplifies Nick Herbig more. Um but I don't think Highsmith and Watt are going to, you know, see some dramatic change. They might see a little less playing time just to keep them healthier. Uh to make sure they're they're kind of like stay fresh throughout the year. I feel like they're in just multiple times throughout the last 2 years I've watched T.J. Watt play 90% of the snaps and by the end of the game he looks gassed. And and you know, they need him for that final drive and that big play. And sometimes it just looks like he doesn't have the juice or the stamina to do it. Highsmith's always been a guy that's been pretty much, you know, full go and even when he's at 80, 85% he's been really good and explosive, but he's been injured, you know, the past two seasons. So, you hope to keep him healthy. Um and so, those two guys, to me, Herbig playing more can help those guys stay healthy. Um and so, I really like that idea. Jack Sawyer can obviously also factor into this. His second year you hope he takes a leap and you really have a forehead monster if he can do that. Um but I don't think there's going to be anything too crazy. I don't think they're going to move one of the edge rushers this year. I think that's going to be in 2027 and as we talked about, there's an absence of information there for which of the two to move. I don't think they're going to uh kind of change the contracts for either of these two. I don't think maybe they add incentives to Highsmith. That's about it. I don't think they're going to touch Highsmith or Watts for future years. So, we'll see where that goes after this season, but I think this season is a very good problem to have to three very good edge rushers. >> A very good problem to have. text: you've had this off seasonason to kind of learn what's going on with these new coaches, this new scheme. But in my mindset when I come back for training camp, I want to be in the best shape of my life to be able to have that mindset. Nah, coach, I could go four more or whatever it may be.
